description: Can we imagine Russia beyond Russian culture and the Russian-dominated history of the country? This course offers students the opportunity to delve into the rich histories and cultures of the Indigenous peoples of North Asia through an examination of historical texts, documentaries, films, and novels. Students will engage with a wide range of Indigenous writings, including pictographic and ideographic texts that have survived Russian colonization and Soviet collectivization, Indigenous autobiographies supported by Orthodox missionaries and Soviet institutions, socialist realist novels, and experimental de- and post-colonial works. We will seek to interrogate these texts within the context of Russian and Soviet history and through the lens of theoretical and ethnographic work relating to the broader Indigenous world.
shortname: Top: Literatures of the Asian North
